title: Classes, new/delete and RAII
summary: Build a growable stack that owns heap memory and cleans up after itself.
hints: The constructor should allocate the first array with `new int[2]` and set `capacity_` to 2. The destructor must release it with `delete[] data_;`. Arrays allocated with `new[]` must be freed with `delete[]`, and mixing them up is undefined behaviour.
To grow: allocate a new array of `capacity_ * 2` ints, copy the `size_` elements across, `delete[]` the old array, then point `data_` at the new one and update `capacity_`. Copy before you delete.
`pop` and `top` on an empty stack must `throw std::out_of_range("...");`. `pop` returns `data_[--size_]`, which shrinks the size and reads the old top in one expression. Check `size_ == 0` first.
